Residue.code:
/-- Hydrophobic (H) and hydrophilic (P) residues. -/
inductive Residue where
  | H
  | P
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

Sequence.code:
/-- An input protein is a finite word over {H,P}; the empty word is allowed. -/
abbrev Sequence := List Residue

Fold.code:
/-- A self-avoiding walk of length N vertices in an arbitrary simple graph.
Only consecutive positions must be adjacent; other positions may also touch. -/
structure Fold {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (N : ℕ) where
  pos : Fin N → V
  injective_pos : Function.Injective pos
  consecutive : ∀ i j : Fin N, i.val + 1 = j.val → G.Adj (pos i) (pos j)

hhBonds.code:
/-- H-H bonds, represented by ordered indices i < j to avoid double counting.
In particular, we do NOT exclude pairs with j = i + 1. -/
def hhBonds (S : Sequence) (f : Fold G S.length) :
    Finset (Fin S.length × Fin S.length) :=
  (Finset.univ ×ˢ Finset.univ).filter fun ij =>
    ij.1 < ij.2 ∧ S.get ij.1 = Residue.H ∧ S.get ij.2 = Residue.H ∧
      G.Adj (f.pos ij.1) (f.pos ij.2)

bondCount.code:
def bondCount (S : Sequence) (f : Fold G S.length) : ℕ :=
  (hhBonds S f).card

cubicLattice.code:
/-- The fixed infinite graph Z³: a step changes exactly one coordinate by ±1. -/
def cubicLattice : SimpleGraph Site where
  Adj x y := latticeDistance x y = 1
  symm := by
    intro x y h
    rw [latticeDistance_comm y x]
    exact h
  loopless := by
    intro x
    simp [latticeDistance]

HPInstance.Accepts.code:
def HPInstance.Accepts (I : HPInstance) : Prop :=
  HPStringFold (G := cubicLattice) I.sequence I.minBonds

PacksCube.code:
/-- Exact filling, not merely containment: every cube site is occupied by H,
and every H is in the cube. Injectivity also excludes P from these sites. -/
def PacksCube (S : Sequence) (f : Fold cubicLattice S.length) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : Site, hydrophobicSites S f = cube a n

PerfectHPStringFold.code:
/-- A total predicate on raw inputs: an incorrect H count makes it false. -/
def PerfectHPStringFold (S : Sequence) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  hydrophobicCount S = n ^ 3 ∧
    ∃ f : Fold cubicLattice S.length, PacksCube S f n

hpEncoding.code:
/-- Section 2's HP STRING-FOLD instance with the graph fixed to Z³.
Format: tagged residues, separator, sign bit, binary magnitude of m.
Length = |S| + 2 + bitlength(|m|); no padding and no unary integer field. -/
def hpEncoding : FinEncoding HPInstance :=
  let e := pairEncoding sequenceEncoding signedEncoding
  { Γ := e.Γ
    ΓFin := e.ΓFin
    encode := fun I => e.encode (I.sequence, I.minBonds)
    decode := fun w => (e.decode w).map (fun sm => ⟨sm.1, sm.2⟩)
    decode_encode := by
      intro I
      rw [e.decode_encode]
      cases I
      rfl }

InNP.code:
/-- The polynomially bounded verifier definition of NP.

The certificate encoder must cover all words over its alphabet. This prevents
an arbitrary encoding image from hiding an undecidable certificate-validity
condition. Ordinary finite-word certificates with `wordEncoding` satisfy this
condition directly. The verifier runs on `pairEncoding ea ec`, whose length is
the input length plus certificate length plus one. Both lengths in the bound
are actual encoding lengths; p has natural coefficients.

This is a predicate definition, not a proof of membership for any HP problem. -/
def InNP {A : Type} (ea : FinEncoding A) (L : A → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ (C : Type) (ec : FinEncoding C),
    Function.Surjective ec.encode ∧
    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (R : A × C → Prop),
      PolyTimeDecidable (pairEncoding ea ec) R ∧
        ∀ x, L x ↔ ∃ c, (ec.encode c).length ≤ p.eval (ea.encode x).length ∧ R (x, c)

NPHard.code:
/-- Universal NP-hardness, not hardness relative to an assumed complete problem.
The source type is in universe zero, just as in mathlib's TM2 computation API. -/
def NPHard {A : Type} (ea : FinEncoding A) (L : A → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (B : Type) (eb : FinEncoding B) (M : B → Prop),
    InNP eb M → KarpReduces eb ea M L

hpStringFold_inNP.code:
/-- HP STRING-FOLD on the fixed cubic lattice belongs to NP (footnote 1).
The polynomial verifier is implemented and its soundness/completeness proved. -/
theorem hpStringFold_inNP : InNP hpEncoding (fun I : HPInstance => I.Accepts)

perfectHPStringFold_inNP.code:
/-- PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD belongs to NP (footnote 1). Raw inputs with the
wrong H count are rejected, exactly as in the frozen problem definition. -/
theorem perfectHPStringFold_inNP :
    InNP perfectEncoding (fun I : PerfectInput => PerfectHPStringFold I.1 I.2)

SATPacking.modifiedBinPackingUnary_NPHar.code:
/-- The strong unary packing source is NP-hard assuming only Cook--Levin.
Every reduction and runtime witness used after that source assumption is
proved, rather than supplied as an additional hypothesis. -/
theorem modifiedBinPackingUnary_NPHard (hCL : CookLevin) :
    Packing.ModifiedBinPackingUnaryNPHard

CubicPacking.packingToPerfect_correct.code:
/-- The implemented total map preserves both yes- and no-instances. -/
theorem packingToPerfect_correct (I : Packing.Instance) :
    Packing.ModifiedAccepts I ↔
      PerfectHPStringFold (packingToPerfect I).1 (packingToPerfect I).2

CubicPacking.packingToPerfect_karp.code:
/-- The actual polynomial-time many-one reduction, with both semantic
directions proved on all raw inputs and no additional assumptions. -/
theorem packingToPerfect_karp :
    KarpReduces Packing.instanceEncoding perfectEncoding Packing.ModifiedAccepts
      (fun I : PerfectInput => PerfectHPStringFold I.1 I.2)

perfect_karpReduces_hp.code:
/-- Theorem 3.2 yields an actual Karp reduction on all raw perfect inputs.
The wrong-H-count cases map to a fixed HP no-instance. -/
theorem perfect_karpReduces_hp :
    KarpReduces perfectEncoding hpEncoding
      (fun I : PerfectInput => PerfectHPStringFold I.1 I.2) (fun I : HPInstance => I.Accepts)

PerfectHPStringFoldNPHard.code:
/-- The main hardness step, Section 2 and Section 3.2 (pp. 31-32):
PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD is NP-hard. Raw inputs with the wrong H count are rejected. -/
def PerfectHPStringFoldNPHard : Prop :=
  NPHard perfectEncoding (fun I : PerfectInput => PerfectHPStringFold I.1 I.2)

perfectHPStringFold_NPHard.code:
/-- PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD is NP-hard, assuming only the explicit Cook--Levin
statement. Every subsequent reduction and its runtime are kernel checked. -/
theorem perfectHPStringFold_NPHard (hCL : SAT.CookLevin) :
    PerfectHPStringFoldNPHard

PerfectHPStringFoldNPComplete.code:
/-- Section 3.2's NP-completeness claim for PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD.
Footnote 1 (p. 31) distinguishes hardness from the additional NP-membership step.
The raw-input formulation uses the same perfect-packing predicate as Section 2. -/
def PerfectHPStringFoldNPComplete : Prop :=
  NPComplete perfectEncoding (fun I : PerfectInput => PerfectHPStringFold I.1 I.2)

perfectHPStringFold_NPComplete.code:
/-- The perfect cubic problem is NP-complete: hardness from the proved
packing reduction, membership from the proved direction-certificate verifier. -/
theorem perfectHPStringFold_NPComplete (hCL : SAT.CookLevin) :
    PerfectHPStringFoldNPComplete

HPStringFoldNPComplete.code:
/-- The paper's main result, announced in Section 2 (p. 31) and Section 3:
HP STRING-FOLD on the fixed cubic lattice Z³ is NP-complete. -/
def HPStringFoldNPComplete : Prop :=
  NPComplete hpEncoding (fun I : HPInstance => I.Accepts)

hpStringFold_NPComplete.code:
/-- The paper's main theorem: HP STRING-FOLD on the unchanged cubic lattice
is NP-complete, using the actual perfect-to-threshold Karp reduction. -/
theorem hpStringFold_NPComplete (hCL : SAT.CookLevin) :
    HPStringFoldNPComplete

SAT.CookLevin.code:
/-- **The Cook–Levin hypothesis**: CNF-SAT (binary indices) is NP-hard in the
project's sense. Use only as an explicit hypothesis. -/
def CookLevin : Prop := NPHard cnfEncoding Satisfiable

HPInstance.code:
/-- The finite input to HP STRING-FOLD when the graph is fixed to Z³. -/
structure HPInstance where
  sequence : Sequence
  minBonds : ℤ
  deriving Repr

PerfectInstance.code:
/-- The well-formed inputs to PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD. A natural side length
implements the meaningful nonnegative integer sizes; zero is permitted. -/
structure PerfectInstance where
  side : ℕ
  sequence : Sequence
  count_eq : hydrophobicCount sequence = side ^ 3

PerfectIffThreshold.code:
/-- Theorem 3.2 of the paper, recorded as a proposition for future proof.
This is a definition of a target, NOT a proof or an axiom. -/
def PerfectIffThreshold : Prop :=
  ∀ I : PerfectInstance,
    I.Accepts ↔ HPStringFold (G := cubicLattice) I.sequence (cubeBondThreshold I.side)

PolyTimeDecidable.code:
/-- A total Boolean decider on encoded inputs, with a polynomial TM2 time bound.
The machine structure is data, so `Nonempty` turns its existence into a Prop.
As in mathlib, behavior outside the image of the input encoding is unspecified. -/
def PolyTimeDecidable {A : Type} (ea : FinEncoding A) (L : A → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : A → Bool,
    Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime ea finEncodingBoolBool f) ∧
      ∀ x, f x = true ↔ L x

KarpReduces.code:
/-- Karp (polynomial-time many-one) reducibility, for independently encoded types.
The reducing function is total and preserves both yes- and no-instances. -/
def KarpReduces {A B : Type} (ea : FinEncoding A) (eb : FinEncoding B)
    (L : A → Prop) (M : B → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : A → B,
    Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime ea eb f) ∧ ∀ x, L x ↔ M (f x)

ThreeDimensionalMatching.cnfToBlockMatch.code:
/-- The source reduction uses the frozen binary CNF encoding and the explicit
unary-universe 3DM encoding, with a proved actual polynomial-time machine. -/
theorem cnfToBlockMatching_karp :
    KarpReduces cnfEncoding instanceEncoding Satisfiable Accepts

MatchingPacking.matching_karpReduces_mod.code:
/-- Correctness and a fully constructed finite-machine polynomial-time witness
for strong unary modified packing, with no source-hardness assumption. -/
theorem matching_karpReduces_modified :
    KarpReduces ThreeDimensionalMatching.instanceEncoding Packing.instanceEncoding
      ThreeDimensionalMatching.Accepts Packing.ModifiedAccepts
